verdict.text: 4 problems App Review or App Store Connect turns away, and 5 warnings to review

findings.title: Purpose string missing
findings.message: permission_handler PERMISSION_CONTACTS (ios/Podfile:48) needs NSContactsUsageDescription (contacts); Runner has none.

fix.title: Add the key to Info.plist
steps: Add the key to the target's Info.plist with one sentence that says what the app does with the data, for example: <key>NSCameraUsageDescription</key><string>Scan the barcode on a receipt to add it to your expenses.</string>
If the app never uses this feature, remove the code or the package that uses it instead.

findings.title: Xcode older than App Store Connect accepts
findings.message: codemagic.yaml pins Xcode 16.4 (xcode key); App Store Connect accepts uploads built with Xcode 26 or later since 28 April 2026.

fix.title: Build with Xcode 26 or later
steps: Change the pinned version to Xcode 26 or later (for example 27.1) in the file and line the finding names, and use a runner or build image that has it.
Fix the build warnings and errors the newer SDK reports before the next upload.

sources.title: Apple Developer News: Upcoming SDK minimum requirements (3 February 2026)

findings.title: Purpose string is placeholder or default text
findings.message: NSCameraUsageDescription "your usage description here" is the sample text from the camera package README.

fix.title: Say why the app needs access
steps: Replace the text with one sentence that names what the app does with the data, for example "Take a photo of your meal to log it" rather than "needs camera access".

sources.title: Apple: Adhere to the requirements for purpose strings

findings.title: Export compliance not declared
findings.message: The Info.plist of Runner has no ITSAppUsesNonExemptEncryption, so App Store Connect asks the export compliance questions for every build.

fix.title: Declare the app's encryption
steps: If the app (with its libraries) uses no encryption, or only the encryption built into the operating system such as HTTPS through URLSession, add <key>ITSAppUsesNonExemptEncryption</key><false/>.
If it uses non-exempt encryption, set it to <true/> and add ITSEncryptionExportComplianceCode with the code Apple gives you after reviewing your documentation.

sources.title: Apple: Complying with Encryption Export Regulations

findings.title: Account creation without account deletion
findings.message: Accounts are created (a createUserWithEmailAndPassword call in lib/main.dart:32), and no account deletion call or "Delete account" text was found in the app's code or strings.

fix.title: Let people delete their account in the app
steps: Add a Delete account action that is easy to find, usually in the account settings, and that deletes the account record with its personal data, not only deactivates it.
If deletion finishes on a website, link straight to that page. With Sign in with Apple, also revoke the user's tokens.
If the app already has it under words reviewready does not know, turn the finding off with --ignore RVW301.

sources.title: Apple: Offering account deletion in your app

findings.title: Third-party login without an equivalent option
findings.message: Google Sign-In is used (the google_sign_in package in pubspec.yaml), and no Sign in with Apple was found: no package, entitlement or AuthenticationServices call.

fix.title: Offer Sign in with Apple next to the other login
steps: Add Sign in with Apple (AuthenticationServices on iOS, sign_in_with_apple on Flutter, expo-apple-authentication or @invertase/react-native-apple-authentication on React Native) and the Sign in with Apple capability.
If the app falls under one of the exceptions of guideline 4.8, or offers another login service with the listed features, turn the finding off with --ignore RVW401.

findings.title: No privacy manifest
findings.message: Runner has no PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy in its resources.

fix.title: Add a privacy manifest to the app target
steps: In Xcode choose File > New > File from Template, pick App Privacy, name it PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy and tick the app target.
Record the data the app collects (NSPrivacyCollectedDataTypes) and the reasons for each required reason API the app's own code uses (NSPrivacyAccessedAPITypes). SDKs ship their own manifests.

sources.title: Apple: Describing use of required reason API
